abstract: A Barnette graph is simple, cubic, $3$-connected, bipartite and planar. It has the global $H^{+-}$ property if, for every ordered pair of distinct edges $(e,f)$, some Hamilton cycle contains $e$ and avoids $f$. This property implies Hamiltonicity, and its facial version is equivalent to Barnette's conjecture by a theorem of Kelmans. All Barnette graphs on at most $66$ vertices are known computationally to have it, and infinite families follow from tight-cut composition. We give a controlled expansion mechanism with an explicit growth rate. Starting from the cube, we iterate legal $C_4$-expansions at two recurrent sites. An exact six-traversal criterion describes the Hamilton cycles of one expansion in terms of parent structures. A finite signed-support invariant (22 states, or 40 when reflected orientations are allowed), initialised by explicit cube witnesses, then shows that every construction word yields a Barnette graph with global $H^{+-}$. A rooted grammar argument shows that depth $k$ produces exactly $2^{\max(k-2,0)}$ boundary-pointwise isomorphism types. A cubic embedding bound turns this into $B_{H^{+-}}(8+4k)\ge\lceil 2^{\max(k-2,0)}/((8+4k)3^{7})\rceil$, so $B_{H^{+-}}(n)\ge 2^{n/4-O(\log n)}$ along $n\equiv 0 \pmod 4$. Exhaustive computer checks agree with these statements for all standard words with $n\le 32$ and all reflected words with $n\le 28$. Limitations: the result concerns two specific expansion sites, not arbitrary $C_4$-expansions. The explicit bound first exceeds $1$ at $n=88$. Nothing is claimed about Barnette's conjecture. A 2005 edge-replacement scheme of Kao and Chen could not be consulted in full, so we make no absolute priority claim. The work was developed with AI assistance and has not been independently reviewed by experts.
author: lihongmin
change_summary:
- Review item 1: Lemma 8.1 now states the signed conditions for all eight final positions explicitly as (7.15a) (role sets Z_j, O_j read from the Hamilton-cycle rows (7.15)); the proof of Theorem 8.2 uses them for older-edge/final-edge pairs. The supplement adds a direct check of (7.15): each role has exactly one final Hamilton completion with the stated row, all 56 ordered final pairs are separated, and all 640 older-edge/new-edge conditions hold for the 40 states.
- Review item 2: Problem and Related work now credit infinite global-H^{+-} families to tight-cut composition (Gorsky-Steiner-Wiederrecht, Lemma 4.5) and present the contribution as a controlled C4-expansion mechanism with an explicit growth rate; added the connection through their Lemma 5.2 (C4-expansion preserves 2-extendability), so every graph of the family is a brace.
- Review item 2: corrected the statement about Kao-Chen: its indexed abstract does state the quantifiers (one-edge and opposite-colour vertex-pair fault tolerance, Hamiltonian laceability); what remains unknown is the replacement gadget.
- Review item 3: the supplement records tested dependency versions, collects garbage between exhaustive searches, and turns printed checks (seed joint separation, cap isomorphism, family results) into assertions that give a nonzero exit status on failure.
- Review item 4: removed nested math delimiters inside display environments and the doubled backslashes in the abstract; the abstract no longer says that no exponentially large family was recorded.
title: Exponentially Many Barnette Graphs with the Global $H^{+-}$ Property
